![By a Lady: First Editions of the Novels of Jane Austen](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/11191433-2831-0139-0000-3d8945a25866:4)
Original first editions of Jane Austen’s novels—`published anonymously in London between 1811 and 1818` —typically sell for tens of thousands to over $100,000 depending on the title, binding, and condition. Early illustrated editions and first editions *thus* (first illustrated by a specific artist) generally range from around $700 to $7,500.[[1]](https://www.christies.com/en/stories/jane-austen-at-250-f1524d1ddc834e09be97b04788654aab)[[2]](https://www.raptisrarebooks.com/product/pride-and-prejudice-jane-austen-first-edition-rare-book/)[[3]](https://www.sothebys.com/en/articles/the-five-most-valuable-jane-austen-books)[[4]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:7646105290843991930&ibp=oshop)[[5]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:10402135437515860064&ibp=oshop)[[6]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:516472045564888894&ibp=oshop)[[7]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:17187055112854585933&ibp=oshop)

### Key First Edition Details

- **Original 19th-Century Printings:** Early editions appeared anonymously (credited as *"By a Lady"* ) in multi-volume sets, such as *Sense and Sensibility* (1811) and *Pride and Prejudice* (1813, in three volumes).[[1]](https://janeaustens.house/object/pride-and-prejudice-first-edition/)[[2]](https://www.sothebys.com/en/articles/the-five-most-valuable-jane-austen-books)
- **Notable Market Examples:** 
	- *Sense and Sensibility* (1811 first edition): Auction estimates often reach $80,000–$120,000 for well-preserved copies.
	- *Mansfield Park* (1814 first edition): Auction estimates commonly range from $30,000–$50,000.
	- *Pride and Prejudice* (1832 first American edition): Listed around $60,000 in a custom fine art binding.
	- *Pride and Prejudice* (1894 first Hugh Thomson "Peacock" illustrated edition): Typically listed around $5,200–$7,480.
	- *Sense and Sensibility* (illustrated editions by C. E. Brock or Hugh Thomson): Often listed between $695 and $2,500.[[1]](https://www.christies.com/en/stories/jane-austen-at-250-f1524d1ddc834e09be97b04788654aab)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:3700182552848650611&ibp=oshop)[[3]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:7646105290843991930&ibp=oshop)[[4]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:2258702539061801165&ibp=oshop)[[5]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:10402135437515860064&ibp=oshop)[[6]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:516472045564888894&ibp=oshop)[[7]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:17187055112854585933&ibp=oshop)

### Where to Browse & Buy

- **Rare Book & Auction Specialists:** Explore listings and auction highlights through [Bauman Rare Books](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/authors/Jane-AUSTEN/203276), [Christie's](https://www.christies.com/en/stories/jane-austen-at-250-f1524d1ddc834e09be97b04788654aab) , and [Harrington Books](https://www.harringtonbooks.co.uk/pages/author/239/jane-austen/?orderBy=).
- **Historical Context:** View archival details on early printings at [Jane Austen's House](https://janeaustens.house/object/pride-and-prejudice-first-edition/).[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/authors/Jane-AUSTEN/203276)[[2]](https://www.christies.com/en/stories/jane-austen-at-250-f1524d1ddc834e09be97b04788654aab)[[3]](https://www.harringtonbooks.co.uk/pages/author/239/jane-austen/?orderBy=)[[4]](https://janeaustens.house/object/pride-and-prejudice-first-edition/)

references.title: [First Edition] Pride and Prejudice, with a Preface by George Saintsbury and Illustrations by Hugh Thomson. [FIRST 'PEACOCK EDITION'] JANE AUSTEN
references.text: FIRST 'PEACOCK EDITION'. Cloth-bound; hardcover; octavo (18.5 x 12 x 3.5 cm); pp. xxvii, 476. English text, the Preface provided by George Saintsbury. Bound in publisher's original blue cloth; elaborately blocked and lettered in gilt to front cover and spine with the famous image of a fully blossomed peacock perched on a sundial; all page edges gilt; coated endpapers; half-title; 160 line drawings by Hugh Thomson including frontispiece with tissue-guard; decorated title-page; facsimile printed inscription: " To J. Comyns Carr, In acknowledgment of all I owe to his friendship and advice, these illustrations are gratefully inscribed. Hugh Thomson." Printed at the Chiswick Press:- Charles Whittingham and Co., Tooks Court, Chancery Lane, London. Condition: VERY GOOD. Binding tight and secure. Slight bumping to spine ends. Points with trivial rubbing. Interior largely fresh and clean, with some light toning to title. Contemporary inscription neatly inked to front endpaper verso. A beautiful copy. Notes: This is the renowned "Peacock Edition" of Austen's classic, which is generally considered to be the finest illustrated interpretation of Jane Austen's popular novel and is presented in one of the most lavish and aesthetically pleasing pictorial gilt bindings of the period. A beautiful copy, illustrated by Hugh Thomson, who was one of the most notable book illustrators of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and his illustrations for Jane Austen's novels remain widely regarded as classics in the field. Known for his attention to detail, Hugh Thomson would often spend a great deal of time in museums researching the lifestyles and dress of the characters he was depicting, Thomson started working on his drawings for "Pride and Prejudice" in 1893. They proved an immense success, selling over 10,000 copies in the few years after they were released. He would go on to illustrate many of Austen's other novels.

references.text: AUSTEN, Jane (1775-1817). Sense and Sensibility. With an introduction by Austin Dobson. Illustrated by Hugh Thomson. London: Macmillan and Co., Limited; New York: The Macmillan Company, 1896. First Edition Thus. First Hugh Thomson-illustrated edition, and the first fully illustrated edition of Sense and Sensibility. Octavo (8vo). xvi, 341 pp, [6] publisher's advertisements. Publisher's original burgundy-red cloth, blind-stamped with floral decoration to both boards, the front board and spine lettered in gilt. Illustrated with 40 full-page line drawings by Hugh Thomson, including a tissue-guarded frontispiece. Introduction by Austin Dobson. Printed by R. & R. Clark, Limited, Edinburgh. An important late-Victorian illustrated edition of Austen's first published novel. Thomson's finely observed Regency-inspired drawings established one of the most recognizable visual interpretations of Austen's world and form part of the celebrated series of illustrated Macmillan Austen editions issued at the end of the nineteenth century. Contents clean with light, even toning and occasional handling marks. Endpapers toned and foxed, with an ownership bookplate to the front pastedown. Binding remains sound and square. Spine cloth sunned, with rubbing to the extremities and light wear at the head and foot; corners gently bumped. A Very Good copy. Reference: Gilson E82. [Attributes: First Edition Thus; Hard Cover; Illustrated.]

references.title: [First Edition] Sense and Sensibility. Austen, Jane
references.text: First deluxe edition of Jane Austen's first published novel, her subtle comedy of the contrasting Dashwood sisters. Octavo, original cloth with the upper cover and spine decorated in gilt with an elaborate floral design and a basket of flowers, top edge gilt, pictorial endpapers, tissue guarded color frontispiece. Beautifully illustrated with twenty-four color illustrations by C. E. Brock.Â In very good condition. A very sharp example. Sense and Sensibility, first published in 1811 by Thomas Egerton of London as Jane Austen's debut novel, is a work of brilliant psychological and social comedy contrasting the temperaments and romantic fortunes of two sisters: the reserved and sensible Elinor Dashwood, who governs her emotions with perfect propriety, and the passionate and impulsive Marianne, who gives herself over to feeling with equally perfect abandon. The novel's central argument, that both pure sense and pure sensibility are insufficient guides to a well-lived life and that some integration of the two is required for genuine happiness, is delivered through one of the most elegantly constructed plots in the Austen canon and a cast of characters whose social comedy has lost none of its freshness across two centuries of continuous readership. The definitive screen adaptation remains Ang Lee's Sense and Sensibility (1995), with a screenplay by Emma Thompson, who also starred as Elinor opposite Kate Winslet's Marianne, Hugh Grant as Edward Ferrars, and Alan Rickman as the devoted Colonel Brandon. The film earned seven Academy Award nominations including Best Picture, and Thompson won the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, making her the only person in history to have won Academy Awards for both acting and screenwriting. The film grossed $135 million worldwide against a $16 million budget and is widely regarded as the gold standard of Austen adaptations.

references.title: [First Edition] Sense and Sensibility. With Twenty-Four Coloured Illustrations by C.E. Brock. AUSTEN, JANE [Used - Near fine] [Hardcover]
references.text: FIRST 'ENGLISH IDYLLS' EDITION. Cloth-bound; hardcover; octavo (19.5 x 12.5 x 3cm); pp. [viii], 308. English text. Publisher's original full cloth; elaborately blocked and lettered in gilt to front cover and spine; t.e.g.; untrimmed fore edge and bottom edge; pictorial endpapers; initial and terminal blanks plus half-title present; framed title-page with vignette; illustrated with 24 full-page coloured plates by C. E. Brock; head-pieces. Printed by The Temple Press. Condition: NEAR FINE. A touch of browning to endpapers and a neat contemporary gift inscription, otherwise a fine example. Scarce thus. Notes: Charles Edmund Brock first illustrated Sense and Sensibility for the edition published by J.M. Dent & Co. in 1898, as part of the novels of Jane Austen in 10 volumes. Sense and Sensibility was published in two volumes for this edition, each with a colour frontispiece and five further plates. For this later edition, Brock produced a new suite of plates, based on watercolour drawings. They are all signed by Brock and dated 1907 or 1908. [Gilson E90 & E120].

Publisher's original full cloth; elaborately blocked and lettered in gilt to front cover and spine; t.e.g.; untrimmed fore edge and bottom edge; pictorial endpapers; initial and terminal blanks plus half-title present; framed title-page with vignette; illustrated with 24 full-page coloured plates by C. E. Brock; head-pieces. Printed by The Temple Press. Condition: NEAR FINE. A touch of browning to endpapers and a neat contemporary gift inscription, otherwise a fine example. Scarce thus. Notes: Charles Edmund Brock first illustrated Sense and Sensibility for the edition published by J.M. Dent & Co. in 1898, as part of the novels of Jane Austen in 10 volumes. Sense and Sensibility was published in two volumes for this edition, each with a colour frontispiece and five further plates. For this later edition, Brock produced a new suite of plates, based on watercolour drawings. They are all signed by Brock and dated 1907 or 1908. [Gilson E90 & E120].

references.title: Jane Austen Pride And Prejudice | First American Edition, Book
references.text: The first US edition, first printing of Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen. Sold as a set of 2 volumes. Jane Austen (English). Philadelphia: Carey & Lea, 1832. 12mo. 199, [1]; 209, [1] pages Publisher's catalogue bound at front of Volume I. Modern full peach design binding by Sol Rébora in Can Can structure with one layer of cotton cloth and two layers of Japanese paper, each element hand-painted with acrylics and textured with a patterned design impressed with deep-relief hot-stamping from silk; spines and boards stamped in dark grey, cotton and abaca handmade paper peach endpapers. First US edition in a stunning fine art binding by the acclaimed Argentinian design bookbinder Sol Rébora. Austen's most beloved novel is simultaneously a unique production of profound artistic confidence and an entertaining popular love story: it builds on a long-established tradition of English courtship novels in conversation with many women authors before her like Frances Burney (from whose book Cecelia Austen may have borrowed the very phrase "pride and prejudice"). Austen admitted in a letter that she thought her book's heroine, Elizabeth Bennett, "as delightful a creature as ever appeared in print" (29 January 1813) – and generations of readers have agreed with her. First published in 1813 in three volumes, this is the first edition to appear in the United States, published in two volumes by Carey & Lea in an edition of only 750 copies. Sol Rébora is an internationally recognized design bookbinder based in Buenos Aires. Her works embody a minimalistic elegance that is nevertheless subtly complex, as in the carefully structured multiple layers used here. They are not only visually stunning, but supremely tactile. From Rèbora's artist statement: "The cloth texture is achieved using silk with a patterned design that evokes the aesthetic of the time period in which the original edition was produced, creating a visual connection with antique paper. This design also appeals to the collective memory of how custom bindings from the early 19th century might have appeared, complete with deep-relief hot-stamping impressions." A magnificent, unique copy of an Austen first. | Jane Austen Pride And Prejudice | First American Edition, Book

references.title: Pride and Prejudice | Austen, Jane | 1894, 1st/1st peacock edition, British issue...
references.text: Publisher and Year: London: George Allen, 1894 Edition: First Peacock edition, first impression, British issue. Title page dated 1894 and copyright page without a printing statement, as called for (later printings would be so stated). One of 11,605 copies. Originally published in 1813, Pride and Prejudice was sparsely illustrated throughout the nineteenth century, with various editions containing only up to six illustrations total. This 1894 edition was the first to be fully illustrated, integrating a full 160 drawings by Hugh Thomson into the text. (Gilson E78) Condition and Description: Octavo (~7.5" x 5"), blue-green cloth, front board and spine elaborately stamped in gilt, all edges gilt, dark blue coated endpapers, frontispiece with tissue guard, 476 pp. Preface by George Saintsbury. As with all copies, a facsimile signature and note by Thomson is on the leaf facing the copyright page. A sturdy and attractive copy. Recased, with very subtle repair to the gutters, spine ends, and the upper inch of the front joint. Hinges and binding quite firm. Light rubbing to the boards, a few handling marks, and a couple of small stains to the rear board. Gilt bright. Edges of the text block a little rubbed. Slight spline lean. Small bookseller ticket to the front pastedown. Price of the book at the time of publication penciled to the verso of the front free endpaper ("6/-"). Christmas gift inscription in ink to the second blank, reading "Catherine Herbert Fullerton / Xmas 1894." No other writing or prior owner markings. Moderate foxing to the preliminary and terminal leaves. Interior pages largely clear, with occasional minor stains and instances of foxing. Provenance: Catherine Herbert Fullerton (1875-1942), who later took the surname of her husband after her wedding in 1898 to the British Olympian athlete, Lt. Henry Alan Leeke (1879-1915). "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife." Inventory ID: 988 - 995 - 183
